title: Spaghetti Puttanesca
subtitle: Tomatoes, olives, capers, and anchovies
excerpt: A quick, intensely flavoured pasta sauce of tinned tomatoes, black olives, capers, anchovies, and chilli. Everything comes from the storecupboard and the whole dish is on the table in 25 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Puttanesca ('whore's style') is a Neapolitan pasta sauce that became popular across Italy in the mid-twentieth century. Its origin is disputed but it is widely associated with Naples and is prized for being made entirely from pantry staples. It is one of the few pasta sauces that improves with a short sit before serving.

recipeTools.notes: Wide enough to reduce the sauce.

content.text: Puttanesca sauce is all storecupboard: tinned tomatoes, black olives, capers, anchovies, garlic, and chilli. The anchovies dissolve into the oil and disappear as fish but leave a savoury backbone. The capers and olives give salt and a slight sharpness. The whole sauce comes together in the time it takes to cook the pasta.

items.preparation: finely sliced, or 0.5 tsp dried chilli flakes

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the anchovies and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, pressing them against the pan with a spoon, until they dissolve into the oil.
Add the garlic and chilli. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the garlic softens.

Add the tinned tomatoes, olives, capers, and oregano. Crush the tomatoes with a spoon and cook on medium heat for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens. Taste, it should be well-seasoned from the anchovies and capers without needing additional salt. Add black pepper.

Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water. Drain, reserving a cup of pasta water. Add the pasta to the sauce and toss, adding a little pasta water if needed. Serve with no cheese, parmesan does not belong here.
